full_judgment: 7. Learned Counsel has placed before us the description of the subject matter of the tenancy as given in the schedule to the plaint of the suit as well as of the decree passed therein, which has been quoted in paragraph 1 of the petition for leave. On a perusal of this description it becomes clear that the suit as well as the decree passed therein were in respect of the land within specified boundaries together with certain structures. In the local investigation which was held for the identity of the decretal premises the Advocate-Commissioner delineated the decretal premises with reference to the survey plots and it is the finding of the Courts below that the decretal land has been correctly described in the petition for execution. We have also examined the description of the premises as quoted in the petition for special leave and we find that it comprised a part of R. S. Plot No. 4953, appertaining to Khatian No. 3695 of Mouza Bakalia, known as Chaletai, with three huts standing thereon, which is the same as the new Municipal holding No. 264, and also the new Municipal holding No. 1863, surrounded on the north by the premises of another, Bharatia, Syed A. Majid. Sowdagar, on the south by that of the other bharatia, Rahman Brothers, on the east by Rajakhali Khal and on the west by the road. It is obvious that the subject matter of the tenancy comprised both lands and huts and as such on the destruction of the huts the entire subject Matter if the tenancy was not destroyed nor did the possession of the tenant in respect of the decretal premises automatically come to an end with such destruction.
